sections.sectionSummaryBrief: On a deeper level, the innovation of simple repentance also relates to the supernal will and intention, drawing forth a new light beyond the original purpose of creation, rooted in the essence of the Ein Sof.

translations.translation: And on a deeper level it can be said,
that the concept of the innovation in repentance in its simple sense is also regarding the will and intention above.
For the will and intention above in the creation of the world and man is that man should be a tzaddik,
as our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said,
"In whom did He consult? In the souls of the tzaddikim."
And by sinning, damaging, and deviating from the path
(the opposite of the intention for the creation of the world and man),
and afterwards rectifying this through repentance,
through this a new light is drawn forth that was not in the intention of creation.
And the power to draw forth a new light that was not in the intention of "in whom did He consult,"
is because the root of the souls is in the Essence of the Ein Sof,
which is above even their root in the concept of "in whom did He consult."
And it can be said,
that this—that through repentance a person changes from his existence and becomes an entirely new existence,
a true innovation that is not a continuation of his previous state—
is,
because through repentance there is a drawing forth of the essence of the soul as it is rooted in the Essence of the Ein Sof,
and regarding the essence of the soul,
the state of the person before repentance makes no difference.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: Based on this, the work of "in sukkot you shall dwell" reveals that through drawing forth the soul's essence via repentance, the encompassing lights are transformed into settled lights.

translations.translation: And based on this, we can add explanation to that which through the service of "in sukkot you shall dwell"
(the revelation of the repentance of Yom Kippur)
a change is made in the encompassing lights, that they become settled lights,
for the concept of drawing forth the essence of the soul through repentance is revealed in that a person changes from his existence,
and therefore,
the revelation of the drawing forth of the Essence through "in sukkot you shall dwell"
(the revelation of the repentance of Yom Kippur)
is in the matter of change,
that encompassing lights are changed to become settled lights.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: The revelation of the soul's essence rooted in the Essence of the Ein Sof through repentance manifests in two aspects: the repentance itself and the cause that brings one to repentance.

translations.translation: And it can be said,
that the revelation of the essence of the soul that is rooted in the Essence of the Ein Sof
(which is above the root of the souls in the concept of "in whom did He consult")
that comes through repentance,
is in two matters.
In the repentance itself and in the cause that brings one to repentance.
And the concept is,
that this—that a person repents after having sinned—is from the aspect of the root of the soul in the Essence of the Ein Sof, which is above the concept of "in whom did He consult."
For from the aspect of the root of the souls in the concept of "in whom did He consult" in the souls of the tzaddikim,
by sinning and damaging
(the opposite of the intention of "in whom did He consult"),
he becomes separated from his root,
and that after sinning he repents and changes his existence,
is from the aspect of the revelation of the root of the soul in the Essence of the Ein Sof,
which is above the concept of "in whom did He consult."
And there is another matter in this,
that the cause that brings him to repent is because the point of Judaism within him is always in perfection
(and when the point of Judaism within him is aroused,
he does not want in any way to be separated, and he repents),
and that the point of Judaism within him is always in perfection,
that even at the time of sin the soul is in trust with Him, blessed be He,
is because the connection of the soul to G-dliness is an essential connection,
which is above the connection through Torah and mitzvos
(the concept of "in whom did He consult").
